Methods note

From data to decisions: four questions to ask of an indicator

Coverage, definition, comparability and uncertainty: a short reading guide for development projects.

An indicator is useful in relation to a specific decision. Before reading a trend, identify what it measures, who is covered and whether the definition has changed.

Comparisons across countries or periods require checks on units, missing observations and breaks in the series. A regional average can hide wide country differences.

Finally, correlation does not establish causation. I communicate findings together with their limitations, assumptions and the additional checks required for a policy decision.

About this note

Original methods note; no new empirical estimate is presented.
